unsupported: The founders, a family team that includes Lionel, began by refusing to send tree material to landfills, instead giving it away as chips and firewood before formalizing the upcycling operation.
All wood comes from Albuquerque’s urban forest—trees removed for instability, disease, or age—and is air-dried for up to two years in the desert climate before milling.
The company cites projects ranging from charcuterie boards and mantles to large conference tables, and notes that its contract milling service accepts logs sourced elsewhere.
